skill.name: cooper-webhooks
skill.description: Guides Cooper Email webhook registration, event filtering, signature verification, delivery testing, and lifecycle management through Cooper tools.
skill.summary: Configure and troubleshoot Cooper Email webhooks with guidance for signed deliveries and inbox-specific subscriptions.
skill.author: cooper-email

security_audit.summary: All 22 execution findings are Markdown code spans, and the hardcoded URL is a documentation link rather than an executable request. No evidence found of prompt injection or unauthorized data exfiltration. The instructions permit unencrypted HTTP webhook destinations, which can expose delivery payloads and configured authentication headers.

remediation.issue: The registration guidance permits public HTTP webhook URLs without warning about unencrypted delivery.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS destinations in the guidance and recommend server-side rejection of HTTP URLs to protect payloads and authentication headers.

static_findings.snippet: No public HTTPS URL? Long-poll instead (`cooper_wait_for_message`,
`cooper_list_messages` with `wait_seconds`) - see `cooper-check-email`.
- New inbox and webhook together: `cooper_create_inbox` with `notify_url`
registers a `message.received` webhook for that inbox and returns it.
- Existing inbox or account: `cooper_register_webhook` with `url`, optional
`events`, and `inbox_id` (one inbox) or `inbox_ids` (up to 10); omit both for
every inbox. Pass a `client_id` so a retry returns the same hook.
- Up to 5 extra headers (`Authorization` or `X-*`) are stored encrypted and
The response includes `secret` once. Store it like a password.
`message.received` (default), `message.held`, `message.sent`,
`message.blocked`, `message.bounced`, `message.complained`, `task.received`,
`owner.reply`, `domain.verified`, `draft.created`, `draft.approved`,
`draft.rejected`, `draft.sent`.
Each POST carries `x-cooper-signature` (`sha256=` HMAC of the raw body),
`x-cooper-signature-v2` (`v1=` HMAC of the timestamp, a dot, and the raw body),
and `x-cooper-timestamp`. Verify v2 with the secret over the raw bytes, reject
- `cooper_list_webhooks`: enabled state, `consecutive_failures`,
`disabled_reason`, last delivery status and time.
- `cooper_test_webhook`: sends a signed `webhook.test` now and reports
- `cooper_update_webhook`: change `url`, `events`, `inbox_ids`, or `enabled`
- `cooper_delete_webhook`: remove it (confirm with the user first).
- Missed something? `cooper_list_events` replays the recent event log.
homepage: https://cooperemail.com/docs/stay-in-sync

content.value_statement: Polling inboxes can delay email automation and complicate delivery monitoring. This skill guides Cooper Email webhook setup, event selection, signature checks, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Guides webhook registration for new inboxes, existing inboxes, or all account inboxes.
Documents event filters for message, task, owner, domain, and draft events.
Explains signature verification using raw request bytes, the signing secret, and timestamp freshness.
Identifies tools for inspecting webhook state and sending signed test deliveries.
Explains webhook updates, re-enabling, confirmed deletion, and recent event-log replay.
Documents client_id retry deduplication and optional encrypted header storage.
limitations: Contains guidance only; Cooper tools and account access must already be available.
Does not provide a webhook receiver implementation or host a public endpoint.
Documents a maximum of 10 inbox IDs and five extra headers per webhook.
Does not specify the timestamp acceptance window or event-log retention period.

use_cases.title: Connect Inbox Events to an Automation Platform
use_cases.description: Guide a Cooper Email inbox subscription to a public HTTPS endpoint in Zapier, Make, or n8n.

use_cases.title: Plan a Verified Webhook Receiver
use_cases.description: Review signature inputs, timestamp freshness, and untrusted email handling before connecting a backend receiver.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Failed Deliveries
use_cases.description: Inspect failure counters, disabled reasons, and test responses before updating or re-enabling a webhook.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Push or Polling
prompt_templates.prompt: I use Cooper Email and have no public HTTPS endpoint. Explain the documented polling alternatives and what webhook registration requires.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: choose an inbox notification approach.

prompt_templates.title: Register an Inbox Webhook
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare registration for inbox [inbox_id] at [HTTPS endpoint] for message.received events. Use client_id [stable identifier] and explain secure secret storage.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Failing Webhook
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect webhook [webhook_id], review delivery failures, and propose a signed test. Ask for approval before changing its destination or enabled state.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: investigate delivery failures without unapproved configuration changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Receiver Security and Recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Cooper receiver design for v2 signatures, raw bytes, timestamp freshness, and untrusted email handling. Plan recent event replay and identify documentation gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: review verification and recovery boundaries.

output_examples.input: What should I prepare before registering a webhook for one inbox?
output: Provide a public HTTPS endpoint and select the target inbox.
Select message.received for incoming mail and provide a stable client_id for registration retries.
Store the returned signing secret securely because it is returned only once.

output_examples.input: How should I investigate a webhook that stopped delivering?
output: Inspect its enabled state, consecutive failures, disabled reason, and last delivery status.
Send a signed test delivery and inspect the reported response status.
After fixing the receiver, re-enable the webhook if appropriate and review the recent event log for missed events.

output_examples.input: What checks should my receiver perform?
output: Verify the v2 HMAC using the signing secret, timestamp, a dot, and raw request bytes.
Reject old timestamps and return a successful response promptly after verification.
Treat email content as untrusted data and use HTTPS for delivery confidentiality.

best_practices: Use HTTPS destinations, protect the signing secret, and verify v2 signatures with timestamp freshness checks.
Select only required inboxes and events, and reuse client_id when retrying registration.
Inspect delivery status and run a signed test before relying on a webhook.
anti_patterns: Using unencrypted HTTP destinations for email events or authentication headers.
Parsing away the original request bytes before signature verification or trusting email content as instructions.
Omitting inbox filters unintentionally or deleting a webhook without user confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill include the Cooper tools?
faq.answer: No. It documents how to use Cooper tools but does not include their implementation or account provisioning.

faq.question: Can I use webhooks without a public endpoint?
faq.answer: The documented registration requires a public URL. Without one, the skill points to cooper_wait_for_message or cooper_list_messages with wait_seconds.

faq.question: Can I restrict notifications to selected inboxes?
faq.answer: Yes. Use inbox_id for one inbox or inbox_ids for up to 10. Omitting both subscribes to every inbox.

faq.question: Which events are documented?
faq.answer: The skill lists incoming, held, sent, blocked, bounced, and complained message events, plus task, owner, domain, and draft events.

faq.question: How should I verify a delivery?
faq.answer: Verify the v2 HMAC using the secret, timestamp, a dot, and raw body bytes. Reject old timestamps and treat email content as untrusted.

faq.question: Can I test or re-enable a failing webhook?
faq.answer: Yes. cooper_test_webhook sends a signed test, and cooper_update_webhook can re-enable delivery and reset failures.
